coverage: Roster: noisms 2019 fetched (on disk, no Le Guin words in it); the Melville blurb traced past every relay to its printed text on The Urth of the New Sun and to a second, earlier Le Guin sentence in Pringle 1985; Guardian obituary NOT FOUND (the 2019 URL 404s, and Le Guin died 2018-01-22, fifteen months before Wolfe, so no Le Guin obituary of him can exist); Steering the Craft and The Language of the Night NOT CHECKABLE at the primary (their official pages carry no table of contents and the Internet Archive lending scans return 403 on fulltext search); Dancing at the Edge of the World, The Wave in the Mind and Words Are My Matter checked by their official tables of contents and contain no Wolfe item; From Elfland to Poughkeepsie read in full as a PDF and does not name Wolfe; public Wolfe-Le Guin correspondence NOT FOUND (part of the Le Guin papers' correspondence is closed until 2069 and the item-level inventory is not on the Archives West page; the Gene Wolfe Collection at Texas A&M holds galleys and one manuscript, no correspondence). Substantive sources by route: named roster 4; bibliography chasing 6 (Edges scan, Interfaces, Norton, Pringle twice, Clute 2009); lateral search 8 (Open Library search-inside, publisher captures, SFE, New Yorker, New Republic, Wikipedia, Archives West, Elfland PDF). Twenty substantive of thirty-one fetched. The literature is genuinely thin and that is the finding: Le Guin never published an essay or review on Wolfe; her whole reachable record on him is one sentence in her 1980 Edges introduction, one three-sentence jacket blurb on The Urth of the New Sun, one sentence quoted by Pringle in 1985, and her editorial acts of selecting Wolfe for three anthologies.
